sections.html:
Newington is a largely residential suburb in Hartford County, about 8 miles south of downtown Hartford, in the Capitol Planning Region. The 2020 census counted 30,536 people on 13.1 square miles, close to 2,326 people per square mile. Neighbors are Hartford, Wethersfield, Rocky Hill, Berlin, New Britain, Farmington and West Hartford.

Streets of houses fill most of the town, with the Berlin Turnpike as the one big commercial strip. Your likely buyers are other Greater Hartford residents.

Wethersfield settlers first took up land on the western edge in 1636. The General Assembly named the place Newington in 1721, but incorporation only came on July 10, 1871. A trolley linked Hartford and New Britain starting in 1894.

The big jump came after the war. Population rose from 5,449 in 1940 to 9,110 in 1950, a leap that tied for the fastest in the state, and reached 17,664 by 1960. Much of the housing you see was built in that wave. Those houses are now several decades old, so an older furnace, wiring or roof is a normal part of a resale.

sections.h2: The Berlin Turnpike and nearby streets
sections.html:
The Berlin Turnpike began as the Hartford and New Haven Turnpike, authorized in 1798, and took its present name in 1942 when it was widened from 18 feet to 200 feet. Small shops have given way to larger chains over the years, with Stew Leonard's, Walmart and Target among the town's top employers. The Connecticut Department of Transportation has its headquarters at 2800 Berlin Turnpike, and Hartford Hospital runs a campus in town.

  • Houses close to the turnpike put shopping and highway access at the door.
  • Interior streets, such as those along Main Street or Willard Avenue, are quieter.
  • Newington Junction holds three historic districts and the Newington Junction Railroad Depot, built in 1870 and on the National Register.

Say where your house sits in relation to these areas when you talk to a buyer.

sections.h2: Mill Pond Falls and local landmarks
sections.html: Mill Pond Falls, a 16-foot natural waterfall in the middle of town, appears on the town seal. Mill Pond Park is open all year, with a path that crosses the falls on a footbridge, and a Waterfall Festival fills the town center every September. Other sites include the Willard Homestead (1730), the General Martin Kellogg House (1808), the National Iwo Jima Memorial on Ella Grasso Boulevard and the Lucy Robbins Welles Library (1939). A buyer is glad to hear that parks and a library are close.

CTfastrak, the state's first bus rapid transit line, opened on March 28, 2015, with a stop at Newington Junction on a separate busway between Hartford and New Britain. Buyers who work in either city often ask about it.

The town center is about 8 miles from Hartford's Union Station.

Newington Public Schools has seven schools. Elizabeth Green, Anna Reynolds, John Paterson and Ruth Chaffee serve kindergarten through grade 4, and children attend the school for their district. Martin Kellogg and John Wallace teach grades 5 through 8, and Newington High School serves grades 9 through 12. Town hall and the police department share the renovated former high school from the 1950s.

An all-volunteer fire department, founded in 1917 and overseen by an elected board of three fire commissioners, covers fire protection. A volunteer ambulance service gives basic life support, with advanced support from American Medical Response at other times.

Under a charter received in 1871, Newington has a council-manager government. A nine-member Town Council serves two-year terms, and an elected mayor presides and votes. The council meets on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month.

For the tax figures on your own account, ask the Revenue Collector's office before closing, and request a payoff that stays good through your closing date.

sections.h2: Conveyance tax for a Newington seller
sections.html:
A conveyance tax attaches to every Connecticut deed. At the base rates it is three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town, one percent in all.

  • The state charges a higher rate on the part of a price over $800,000.
  • The seller's attorney or agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded.
  • Exempt transfers on the state's list include those between spouses and a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence.

Ask the Newington Town Clerk whether an additional municipal rate applies.

Most Newington owners choose between a traditional listing and a direct cash sale.

  • A listing reaches a wide set of buyers and includes showings, inspections and financing contingencies.
  • A cash sale usually closes faster, with no financing contingency.
  • Cash Home Buyers buys houses in Newington as they are, deferred repairs included.

Send your address and condition details and we will respond with an offer you can weigh against a listing.

1. Decide on an offer and a closing date.
  2. The title company or attorney searches the title and orders a payoff from your lender.
  3. You confirm any tax balance with the Revenue Collector.
  4. You sign the deed, Form OP-236 and the tax go in at recording, and the proceeds reach you after payoffs.

Bring photo ID and recent mortgage and tax statements. A postwar house often has papers scattered over decades, so look for permits, receipts for a new roof or furnace, and any survey. Empty the house, hand over keys and openers, and keep your homeowner's policy in force until the deed is recorded.

faqs.a: In Hartford County, about 8 miles south of Hartford. It borders Hartford, Wethersfield, Rocky Hill, Berlin, New Britain, Farmington and West Hartford.

faqs.q: How many people live in Newington?
What major employers are in Newington?
faqs.a: Hartford Hospital's Newington campus is the largest, with 1,481 employees, followed by the Town of Newington and the Connecticut Department of Transportation.

faqs.q: Is there public transit in Newington?
faqs.a: Yes. CTfastrak has a Newington Junction stop, and Connecticut Transit routes 41, 45, 47 and 69 and the 907 Newington Express serve the town.

faqs.q: How much conveyance tax do I owe selling in Newington?
faqs.a: At base rates it is one percent of the price for a house: three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter to the town. A higher state rate applies above $800,000.
